Dear Phil,

I am calibrating a unidimensional GRM model and have a couple questions that I'd love your thoughts on when you have time.

Q1: I ran two different unidimensional GRM models (irt2 and irt3, below) that only differ in the SE estimation method. The first model (irt2) uses S-EM to estimate SEs; whereas, the second model uses the default Oakes method. The Oakes method does not produce any warnings, but the S-EM method states the warning below "could not invert information matrix; model is not likely empirically identified". Do you know why this might be happening? The call and output for each model are below.

Q2: The G2 RMSEA value shows 0, but this seems odd. Do you know if this is indicative of a problem with my model? Any guidance on this is much appreciated--thank you!

Keri

No, you could use the base M2() collapsing, which works quite well in most circumstances. C2 is a special variant when you run out of degrees of freedom in some models and only want to collapse the bivariate relationships rather than the univariate proportions into "scores") (the function in mirt is also broken on the current 1.29 version, so you should install the dev version on Github if you want the correction).

Phil
